claim: The experiments use seven real-world datasets: ECL, ETT (four subsets), Exchange, Traffic, Weather, Solar‑Energy, and PEMS (four subsets).
rationale: The data registry includes ETT hour/minute variants, Solar, and PEMS; experiment scripts cover ECL, Exchange, Traffic, Weather, Solar-Energy, and PEMS03/04/07/08.

claim: The forecasting experiments use prediction lengths S∈{12,24,36,48} for PEMS and S∈{96,192,336,720} for the other datasets, with a fixed lookback length T=96.
rationale: PEMS experiment scripts set seq_len=96 and pred_len to 12, 24, 48, and 96; they do not use 36 as claimed.

claim: The iTransformer framework is applied to Transformer and its variants Reformer, Informer, Flowformer, and FlashAttention.
rationale: The README describes applying the inverted framework to Transformer variants; corresponding inverted model implementations exist for Reformer, Informer, Flowformer, and Flashformer.

claim: Applying the iTransformer framework yields an average performance promotion of 38.9% on Transformer, 36.1% on Reformer, 28.5% on Informer, 16.8% on Flowformer, and 32.2% on FlashAttention.
rationale: The repository figure shows per-dataset promotion values, but does not establish the exact aggregate percentages stated in this claim.

claim: During training, the model randomly selects a subset of variates in each batch and trains only on the selected variates, while still predicting all variates during inference.
rationale: The efficient-training branch samples variates per batch and slices inputs/targets; test inference uses the full variate tensors.

claim: In the iTransformer architecture, attention is applied on the variate dimension and feed‑forward networks are applied on the temporal dimension.
rationale: The model inverts B,L,N to variate tokens B,N,E before encoder attention; temporal history is embedded into each variate representation before feed-forward processing.

claim: AutoTimes processes timestamps in textual form rather than numerical encoding.
rationale: The README documents textual timestamp embeddings and the preprocessing dataset constructs timestamp strings as natural-language prompts.

claim: AutoTimes obtains embeddings for the special token <EOS> using a large language model to capture the embedding for the entire sentence.
rationale: The code tokenizes timestamp text, runs LLaMA, and selects the last hidden state; it sets EOS as the padding token but does not explicitly append or select an EOS token.

claim: The initial learning rate used for training is chosen from the set {10⁻³, 5×10⁻⁴, 10⁻⁴}.
rationale: The Solar long-term training script uses learning_rate=0.000005, which is outside the claimed set.

claim: The batch size used during training is chosen from the set {256, 1024, 2048}.
rationale: The Weather long-term training script uses batch_size=384, which is outside the claimed set.

claim: The number of training epochs is set to 10.
rationale: The Solar long-term training script uses train_epochs=2.

claim: SegmentEmbedding and SegmentProjection are implemented either as a linear layer or as a multilayer perceptron (MLP).
rationale: AutoTimes selects nn.Linear when mlp_hidden_layers is zero and MLP otherwise for the encoder/decoder projections.
